Campus Placement Resume Guide

Campus placement resumes get screened twice — once by your college placement cell, and again by each company's own ATS or recruiter. Both are looking for slightly different things.

Guided Resume BuilderResume Score Checker

What placement cells typically require

  • •CGPA/percentage prominently and accurately stated (many companies hard-filter on this)
  • •A consistent format across the batch, since placement cells often standardize resumes
  • •Complete, verifiable academic timeline with no gaps left unexplained

What company ATS and recruiters look for beyond that

  • •Relevant coding platform scores (LeetCode, HackerRank, Codeforces) for technical roles
  • •Internship and academic project detail — treat these as your "work experience" section
  • •Certifications (NPTEL, Coursera, vendor certifications) relevant to the role
  • •Keyword alignment to the specific job role/track you're applying for, not just "software developer"

Common fresher resume mistakes

  • •Listing every course from the syllabus instead of relevant coursework only
  • •Vague project descriptions with no tech stack or outcome mentioned
  • •Objective statements that say nothing role-specific ("seeking a challenging position")
  • •Two-page resumes — freshers should almost always stay to one page

Frequently asked questions

Should freshers include a resume objective?

A short, role-specific summary can help, but skip generic filler — if it doesn't mention the target role or a specific strength, cut it and use the space for a project bullet instead.

How do I stand out with no work experience?

Depth beats breadth — one or two well-explained projects with real technical detail and outcomes outperform a long list of shallow ones.
